findings.title: A rejected device can authenticate on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before attempting the database write. When the limit is reached, that write fails but the cache entry remains; on the next request, the cache-hit path returns nil without checking the store, so `Authenticate` grants the anonymous identity. A client denied by the limit can therefore bypass it for the cache lifetime by retrying.

findings.title: Concurrent registrations can exceed the configured device limit
findings.body: The device count and subsequent insert are separate database operations with no transaction or lock protecting the check-and-insert. If the count is one below the limit, concurrent requests for different devices can both observe capacity and both insert, leaving the active device count above the configured limit. Enforce the limit atomically if it is intended to be a hard cap.
